mainTopic: Why salting is indispensable despite רב's repetition rule, and which items on the מזבח need salt
overview: רב taught that a rite is indispensable (מעכב) only when the תורה repeats it. The גמרא challenged him from a ברייתא: salt is never repeated, yet the ברייתא treats it as indispensable because it is called a 'ברית'. רב יוסף answers that רב follows our משנה, which says 'לא מלח – כשר'. אביי argues that the משנה only means a זר did the salting. רב יוסף replies that a זר could never approach the מזבח. A second answer says the word 'ברית' counts as if the פסוק had repeated it. The גמרא then asks whether the פסוק 'וכל קרבן מנחתך במלח תמלח' is itself a repetition. It answers that every word of that פסוק is needed by a ברייתא to teach which items need salt: anything burned on the מזבח with wood, but not wood itself, not blood, and not the part of the מנחה the כהנים eat. The גמרא then works through that ברייתא using כלל ופרט וכלל, and asks why blood, rather than the limbs of an עולה, is the item left out. It ends by showing that the limbs share six features with a מנחה (א״ש בנטמ״א).

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: salt is indispensable
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא used against רב finishes. רבי יהודה says the word 'ברית' is stated about salt. רבי שמעון learns from the shared words 'ברית עולם' that just as קרבנות need כהונה, they need salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A covenant is stated about salt,' says רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון says: here it says 'an everlasting covenant of salt,' and there it says 'a covenant of everlasting priesthood.' Just as there can be no קרבנות without כהונה, there can be no קרבנות without salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that shows salt is absolutely required for קרבנות. This is the source being used to challenge רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said a rite is indispensable only if the תורה repeats it. Salt is never repeated, yet both תנאים here treat it as indispensable: רבי יהודה because of the word 'ברית', and רבי שמעון by comparing it to כהונה. So this ברייתא seems to go against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Covenant; something permanent and binding
Salt, which the תורה requires to be put on קרבנות
Priesthood; the service done by כהנים
Offerings brought on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a brand-new topic. It is the second half of a ברייתא the גמרא already started quoting as a challenge to רב.

phrases.english: A covenant is stated regarding salt,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Shimon says:
It is said here: 'It is an everlasting covenant of salt,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:19

phrases.english: and it is said there: 'A covenant of everlasting priesthood' —
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:13, said about פנחס.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְקׇרְבָּנוֹת בְּלֹא כְּהוּנָּה,
phrases.english: just as it is impossible for offerings without priesthood,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְקׇרְבָּנוֹת בְּלֹא מֶלַח.
phrases.english: so too it is impossible for offerings without salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא the גמרא began quoting earlier as a challenge to רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that only rites the תורה repeats are indispensable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Salt is not repeated, yet it is indispensable, so repetition cannot be the only test.

steps.title: רב follows the תנא of our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף defends רב. He says רב agrees with the תנא of our משנה, who says a מנחה with no salt is still כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב holds like our תנא, who said: if he did not salt it, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the challenge from the ברייתא. He says רב simply follows a different תנא, the one in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says salt is indispensable, but our משנה lists 'לא מלח' among the things that do not disqualify a מנחה. So רב has a תנא to rely on, and the ברייתא is no longer a problem for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא; the author of our משנה
He holds; this is his opinion
Valid; the offering still counts

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Rav holds in accordance with our tanna,
who said: if he did not salt it, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different תנא: רב relies on the opinion of our משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves salt is indispensable, which goes against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה holds salt is not indispensable, and רב follows it.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה means a זר did the salting
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects. The same משנה also says 'לא יצק' is כשר, and pouring oil is surely indispensable. So the משנה must mean a זר did it instead of a כהן, and the same applies to salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, does 'he did not pour' also mean he did not pour at all? Rather, it means a כהן did not pour but a זר did. Here too, a כהן did not salt but a זר did.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב יוסף's reading of the משנה. He says the משנה never meant that the salt was left out completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring oil is repeated in the תורה, so even רב agrees it is indispensable. So 'לא יצק' in the משנה cannot mean no oil at all. It must mean a זר poured it instead of a כהן. By the same logic, 'לא מלח' means a זר salted it, and our משנה gives רב no support.

keyTerms.meaning: Poured, the pouring of oil onto the מנחה
A non-כהן
If so; introduces a problem with what was just said
At all

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say a זר is allowed to do the main עבודה. He says that for these particular steps, if a זר did them the מנחה is still כשר. That is what the משנה means.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If so, 'he did not pour' too —
does it mean he did not pour at all?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: לֹא יָצַק כֹּהֵן אֶלָּא זָר,
phrases.english: Rather: a priest did not pour, but a non-priest did,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי: לֹא מָלַח כֹּהֵן אֶלָּא זָר.
phrases.english: here too: a priest did not salt, but a non-priest did.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's reading of the משנה in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's claim that our משנה holds salt is not indispensable
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same משנה lists pouring oil, which is surely indispensable. So the משנה must be talking about who did the act, not whether it was done at all.

steps.title: A זר could never approach the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers אביי. Salting the קומץ happens at the מזבח, where a זר may not go. So 'לא מלח' cannot mean a זר salted it; it must mean no salt at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Could it enter your mind that a זר would approach the מזבח?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his reading of the משנה against אביי's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For pouring oil, which is done away from the מזבח, אביי's 'a זר did it' reading works. But salting the קומץ is done at the מזבח, where a זר cannot go. So for salt, the משנה must mean that no salt was used at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it really enter your mind? A way of calling an idea impossible
Approaches the מזבח
The altar

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is answering אביי.

phrases.english: But could it enter your mind
that a non-priest would approach the altar?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תַּעֲלֶה עַל דַּעְתְּךָ שֶׁזָּר קָרֵב לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection in step 3 and restores רב יוסף's answer from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes salt from pouring: salt is done at the מזבח, where a זר cannot go
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לא מלח' means a זר did the salting, like 'לא יצק'.
steps.terutzMaskana: A זר cannot salt at the מזבח, so 'לא מלח' means no salt at all, and the משנה supports רב.

steps.title: The word 'ברית' counts as a repetition
steps.stepSummary: A second answer for רב: because the תורה calls salt a 'ברית', it counts as if the פסוק had repeated it. So salt fits רב's rule after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: since 'ברית' is written about it, it is as if a פסוק had repeated it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to defend רב, without relying on our משנה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer agrees that salt is indispensable. It explains that the word 'ברית' does the same job as a repetition. So רב's rule stays intact, and the ברייתא no longer contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say; introduces a second answer
As if the פסוק had repeated it
It is like; it is treated as

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to defend רב. (1) רב follows our משנה, where 'לא מלח – כשר' means no salt at all, since a זר could not salt at the מזבח. (2) The word 'ברית' counts as a repetition, so salt really is indispensable even according to רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: The second answer shows that the word 'ברית' carries the same weight as a repetition in the תורה when deciding whether a rite is indispensable.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
since 'covenant' is written about it,
it is like a case where the verse repeated it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיבָא בֵּיהּ בְּרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the challenge in step 1, instead of the answer in steps 2 to 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broadens what counts as a repetition: the word 'ברית' works like a repeated פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Salt is not repeated, so according to רב it should not be indispensable.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ברית' counts like a repetition, so salt is indispensable even according to רב.

steps.title: Doesn't the תורה already repeat salt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that salt is not repeated in the תורה by quoting the פסוק 'וכל קרבן מנחתך במלח תמלח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that the פסוק does not repeat salt? But it is written: 'And every meal offering of yours you shall season with salt'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the starting point of Step 5. It points to a פסוק that seems to mention salt a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole challenge to רב assumed that salt is never repeated in the תורה. If a פסוק openly mentions salt again, salt already fits רב's rule, and the ברייתא was never a problem for him. The גמרא wants to know why this פסוק does not count as the repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse repeated it (mentioned it a second time)
Salt
But isn't it written...

phrases.english: And the verse does not repeat it?
But isn't it written:
"And every meal offering of yours you shall season with salt"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the premise of the challenge in step 1, that salt is never repeated in the תורה, and questions it. That premise underlies both answers, in steps 2–4 and in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תורה does not repeat the salt command
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק plainly mentions salt again, so the repetition already exists without needing the word 'ברית'

steps.title: That verse is needed to exclude wood and blood
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed for a ברייתא's lesson: the word 'מנחה' limits salting to things that need other items brought for them, which leaves out wood and blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: Had the פסוק said only 'offering with salt', I would think even wood and blood need salt, since they are also called 'offering'. So the פסוק says 'meal offering': just as a מנחה is special because other things are brought as a requirement for it, so too anything that has other things brought as a requirement for it needs salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this פסוק is not a repetition, because every word of it is used for a different lesson. It starts quoting a ברייתא that shows this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that is busy teaching a new lesson cannot also count as a repetition. The word 'קרבן' alone could include wood and blood, but adding 'מנחה' sets a test: salt goes only on something that needs other items, like wood, brought for it. Wood does not need wood, and blood does not need wood, so both are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different lesson)
Wood and blood
Special, having a unique feature
Brought as a requirement for it
The verse teaches (by saying...)

phrases.english: That one is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא:
Had it said only "offering with salt,"
I would understand even wood and blood
which are called "offering."
So the verse says: "meal offering",
just as a meal offering is special
in that other things come as a requirement for it,
phrases.notes: For example, wood has to be brought to burn the קומץ of the מנחה.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁאֲחֵרִים בָּאִין חוֹבָה לָהּ.
phrases.english: so too anything that other things come as a requirement for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 by showing the פסוק is used for other lessons
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is needed for a different lesson, so it is not a repetition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק 'וכל קרבן מנחתך במלח תמלח' is a second mention of salt
steps.terutzMaskana: Its words teach which items need salt, so it does not count as a repetition

steps.title: Maybe blood should need salt, since it permits
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a different shared feature: a מנחה permits the rest to be eaten, so anything that permits, like blood, should need salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe: just as a מנחה is special because it permits, so too anything that permits needs salt. Then I would include blood, which permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a challenge to its own comparison. It suggests a different way to compare, which would bring blood back in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning the קומץ permits the כהנים to eat the rest of the מנחה. Sprinkling the blood of an animal קרבן also permits its meat. If 'permitting' is the shared feature, blood would need salt after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Permits (makes the rest allowed to eat)
I will include
Or perhaps, just as... (suggesting a different comparison)

phrases.english: Or perhaps: just as a meal offering is special in that it permits,
phrases.notes: Burning the קומץ allows the כהנים to eat the rest of the מנחה.

phrases.english: so too anything that permits,
I will include blood, which permits –
phrases.notes: Sprinkling the blood is what allows the meat of an animal קרבן to be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison in Step 7 by proposing a different shared feature
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that blood does not need salt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מנחה can be compared by a different feature, 'permitting', which blood also has

steps.title: "From your meal offering" and not from your blood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the same פסוק: salt must not be missing 'from your meal offering', and that excludes blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'from your meal offering', and not from your blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own challenge with another phrase from the same פסוק. That phrase points to the מנחה and leaves blood out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another word of the פסוק, 'מנחתך', clearly keeps salt with the מנחה and away from blood. So the 'permitting' comparison cannot bring blood back in. This shows again that the words of this פסוק are busy teaching lessons.

keyTerms.meaning: From upon your meal offering
Your blood

phrases.english: The verse says: "from your meal offering,"
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, ויקרא 2:13: don't let the salt be missing from your מנחה.

phrases.english: and not from your blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood needs salt because it permits, like the מנחה

steps.title: Does the whole meal offering need salt?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the entire מנחה needs salt, including the part the כהנים eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the entire meal offering needs salt?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new possibility to set up its next lesson: maybe all of the מנחה needs salt, not just the part burned on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the ברייתא decided which kinds of items need salt. Now it asks how much of the מנחה itself needs it. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think
All of it, the whole thing
Requires

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל תְּהֵא מִנְחָה כּוּלָּהּ טְעוּנָה מֶלַח?
phrases.english: One might think the entire meal offering requires salt?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל תְּהֵא מִנְחָה כּוּלָּהּ טְעוּנָה מֶלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which items need salt to how much of the מנחה needs salt
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the whole מנחה, including the remainder, require salt?

steps.title: Only the part offered on the altar needs salt
steps.stepSummary: The word 'קרבן' teaches that only the part offered on the מזבח, the קומץ, needs salt, not the whole מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'offering': the offering needs salt, but the whole meal offering does not need salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the word 'קרבן' in the פסוק. Only the part that is actually offered needs salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קרבן' means the part brought onto the מזבח, which for a מנחה is the קומץ. The rest, which the כהנים eat, does not need salt. Now every word of the פסוק has its own lesson, which is why it does not count as a repetition for רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Offering; here, the part actually brought onto the מזבח
Requires salt

steps.whatToRemember: The words of 'וכל קרבן מנחתך במלח תמלח' are busy teaching lessons. Wood and blood need no salt, and only the קומץ of a מנחה needs salt. So this פסוק is not a repetition, and רב still needs one of the earlier answers: steps 2–4 or the 'ברית' answer of step 5.

phrases.english: The verse says: "offering,"
the offering requires salt,
but the entire meal offering does not require salt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר קׇרְבַּן קׇרְבָּן טָעוּן מֶלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10. The ברייתא continues in steps 12–15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the קומץ, the part offered as a קרבן, needs salt; the remainder does not

steps.title: What about the frankincense?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that so far only the קומץ of a מנחה needs salt, and asks where we learn that the לבונה needs it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know that the handful of a meal offering needs salt. From where do I learn to include the frankincense?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes one step past what it just learned and asks whether the לבונה also needs salt. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 limited salting to the part of a מנחה that goes on the מזבח, the קומץ. But the לבונה (frankincense) is also burned on the מזבח, so the ברייתא asks if it is included too.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour scooped from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
Frankincense, placed on many מנחות and burned on the מזבח
From where do we learn to include…?
I only know this much so far

phrases.english: And I have only the handful of a meal offering;
from where is it derived to include the frankincense?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא קוֹמֶץ מִנְחָה, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַלְּבוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 11's limit (only the קומץ) and asks whether the rule reaches further.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the לבונה burned with a מנחה also needs salt, and from what source.

steps.title: Frankincense is included because it shares the same vessel
steps.stepSummary: The לבונה is included because it is brought together with the מנחה in one כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include the frankincense, because it comes together with the meal offering in one vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the לבונה needs salt too. It counts as part of the מנחה because they are brought together in the same כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new פסוק is needed here. The לבונה travels with the מנחה in one כלי, so it is treated as part of that same קרבן and shares its salting rule.

keyTerms.meaning: I include (by logic)
One vessel
Since / because

phrases.english: I include the frankincense,
since it comes with it in one vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי אֶת הַלְּבוֹנָה, שֶׁכֵּן בָּאָה עִמָּהּ בִּכְלִי אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The לבונה is included because it is brought in the same כלי as the מנחה, so it counts as part of that קרבן.

steps.title: What about everything else burned on the altar?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists many items that do not come in one כלי with a מנחה and asks where we learn that they need salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn to include frankincense brought by itself, the frankincense in the bowls, the incense, the meal offering of priests, the meal offering of the anointed priest, the meal offering of libations, the sacrificial portions of the sin offering, the guilt offering, the most sacred offerings and the lesser offerings, the limbs of the burnt offering, and the bird burnt offering? From where?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks about a long list of things burned on the מזבח that the 'same vessel' reasoning cannot cover. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning in step 13 only works for לבונה that comes together with a מנחה. Everything on this list either comes alone, is not a מנחה with a קומץ at all, or comes from an animal or bird. So we still need a source for them.

keyTerms.meaning: The two bowls of frankincense placed with the לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
The incense offered in the בית המקדש
The daily מנחה of the כהן גדול
The flour offering that comes along with the wine libations
The fats and parts of an animal offering burned on the מזבח
A burnt offering of a bird

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'מנין' here means the ברייתא doubts these items need salt. It is setting up a single פסוק that covers all of them together.

phrases.english: From where is it derived to include the frankincense
that comes by itself,
phrases.notes: This is someone who pledged to bring just frankincense, with no מנחה at all.

phrases.english: and frankincense that comes in bowls, and the incense,
the meal offering of priests, and the meal offering of the anointed priest,
and the meal offering of libations,
the sacrificial portions of the sin offering, and the sacrificial portions of the guilt offering,
and the sacrificial portions of the offerings of the most sacred order,
and the sacrificial portions of offerings of lesser sanctity,
and the limbs of the burnt offering, and the bird burnt offering: from where?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַלְּבוֹנָה הַבָּאָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 13's 'same vessel' reasoning cannot reach these other items, so a new source is needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for salting all the other items burned on the מזבח that do not come in one כלי with a מנחה.

steps.title: All offerings need salt: 'With all your offerings'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'על כל קרבנך תקריב מלח' includes every item on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'With all your offerings you shall sacrifice salt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the words 'כל קרבנך'. These words include everything burned on the מזבח, so every item on the list needs salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כל' (all) widens the rule beyond the מנחה to every קרבן that goes on the מזבח. This finishes the ברייתא. It shows that the פסוק about salt is fully used to teach which items need salt.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
With all your offerings
Salt

steps.whatToRemember: Everything burned on the מזבח needs salt. The קומץ is learned from 'קרבן', the לבונה because it shares one כלי with the מנחה, and everything else from 'כל קרבנך'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This whole ברייתא is the reason step 7 said the פסוק about salt is 'needed' for its own lesson. Since it teaches which items need salt, it cannot also be used as an extra repeat.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"With all your offerings you shall sacrifice salt."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:13

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר עַל כׇּל קׇרְבָּנְךָ תַּקְרִיב מֶלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14's question and closes the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'כל קרבנך' include every item burned on the מזבח in the requirement of salt.

steps.title: Why do we need the 'one vessel' reason for the frankincense?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that the לבונה is included because it comes in one כלי with the מנחה. It then challenges this, because the ברייתא already taught a broad rule that includes the לבונה anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: I only have the קומץ. Where do we learn to include the לבונה? I include it because it comes with the מנחה in one כלי. But you already said: just as a מנחה is special because other things are brought as a requirement for it (so anything like that needs salt)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא and then asks why that line is needed, since an earlier rule in the ברייתא already covers the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא also taught that anything like a מנחה, meaning anything that needs other items brought for it, needs salt. The לבונה is burned with wood, so that broad rule already includes it. So why does the ברייתא need a separate reason, 'it comes in one כלי'?

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
Frankincense that is brought with a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
One vessel; the לבונה and the מנחה are brought together in it
Special, having a unique feature
Other items are required to be brought for it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא קוֹמֶץ (מִנְחָה),
phrases.english: The Master said: I only have the handful (of a meal offering).

phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא's own broad rule from earlier, which already covers anything burned with wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's derivation and challenges it as repeating something already taught
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's 'one כלי' reason for including the לבונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's broad rule, 'anything like a מנחה that needs other items,' already includes the לבונה, so the extra reason is not needed.

steps.title: The first stage: a generalization and a detail would limit salt to a meal offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the line 'I only have the קומץ' describes the reading of the פסוק as a plain כלל ופרט. That reading would limit salt to a מנחה and nothing else.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: you might say 'קרבן' is a כלל and 'מנחה' is a פרט. With a כלל ופרט, the כלל includes only what is in the פרט. So a מנחה needs salt, and nothing else does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the challenge. It says the ברייתא's 'I only have' line comes from the first stage of reading the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of כלל ופרט says a general word followed by a specific word covers only the specific item. If the פסוק stopped here, only a מנחה would need salt. That is why the ברייתא asked 'from where do we learn the rest?'

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means; the גמרא is explaining the speaker's intent
A general term in a פסוק
A specific term in a פסוק

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
Say "offering" is a generalization,
and "meal offering" is a detail.
With a generalization and a detail,
the generalization includes only what is in the detail.
A meal offering, yes;
anything else, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the challenge in step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא's words as one stage of a step-by-step derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'I only have the קומץ' line seemed to come after the broad rule was already known.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line describes the plain כלל ופרט stage, which would limit salt to a מנחה.

steps.title: The second generalization widens the rule to anything like a meal offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק then adds 'על כל קרבנך,' a second כלל. This creates a כלל ופרט וכלל, which includes anything similar to the מנחה, meaning anything that needs other items brought for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the פסוק says 'על כל קרבנך.' It went back and made a כלל. With a כלל ופרט וכלל, you include only things like the פרט. Just as the פרט that is spelled out is something other items are required for, so too anything that other items are required for needs salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It shows that the end of the פסוק turns the limited reading into a wider one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second general term after the detail widens the rule beyond the detail, but only to things that resemble it. The feature that matters is that a מנחה needs other items brought for it. So the broad rule is the end point of the derivation, and the 'I only have' line was just the earlier stage.

keyTerms.meaning: It went back and made a general statement again
General, specific, general: include only things similar to the specific item
Similar to the specific item
Spelled out clearly in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Plain כלל ופרט means only a מנחה needs salt. כלל ופרט וכלל means anything like a מנחה, something that needs other items brought for it, needs salt.

phrases.english: it went back and generalized.
With a generalization, a detail, and a generalization,

Just as the detail that is spelled out
is something that other things come as a requirement for,

phrases.english: so too anything that other things come as a requirement for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the broad rule is the second stage of the derivation, so there is no repetition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the second כלל, salt would apply only to a מנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second כלל widens the rule to anything that needs other items brought for it.

steps.title: What are the 'other items' required for a meal offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the 'other items brought as a requirement' for a מנחה are.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other things that come as a requirement for it, what are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question to define the key feature it just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole כלל ופרט וכלל depends on the feature 'other items are required for it.' Before the rule can be applied, we need to know which items that phrase refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: What are they?
Other items

phrases.english: The other things that come as a requirement for it,
what are they?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים דְּבָאִין חוֹבָה לָהּ, מַאי נִיהוּ

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which items are the 'others' required for a מנחה

steps.title: The other items are the wood, so anything burned with wood needs salt
steps.stepSummary: The 'other items' are the wood used to burn the קומץ. So anything that needs wood to be burned on the מזבח needs salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wood. So too, anything that needs wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the other items are the wood. This gives the final, practical rule for salting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ cannot be burned without wood, so the wood is the 'required item.' Anything else burned on the מזבח with wood, like the לבונה, fits the same pattern and needs salt.

keyTerms.meaning: Wood, used to burn things on the מזבח
So too, anything

steps.whatToRemember: Anything burned on the מזבח with wood needs salt, because it is like the מנחה, whose קומץ needs wood to be burned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the abstract rule into a clear test: if it is burned with wood on the מזבח, it needs salt.

phrases.english: Wood.
So too, anything that needs wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The required items are the wood, so anything that needs wood on the מזבח needs salt.

steps.title: Why not say the 'other items' are the frankincense, and include blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the 'other items' are the לבונה. If so, blood would be included too, since נסכים come along with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not say that the 'other items that come as a requirement' for the מנחה are the לבונה? Then we would include blood as needing salt, since blood comes with נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 20, which said the 'other items' are the wood. It offers a different reading: the 'other items' are the לבונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the key feature were 'something that comes with an extra item,' then blood would qualify, because wine נסכים come with an animal קרבן. That would mean blood needs salt. This is a real challenge to the wood explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, which is placed on the מנחה
Wine (and flour-oil) libations that come with animal offerings
And bring in, meaning include it in the rule

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא (אֲחֵרִים דְּבָאִין חוֹבָה לָהּ נִיהוּ) – לְבוֹנָה,
phrases.english: Say that the other items that come as a requirement for it are the frankincense,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The meaning is the same either way.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'other items' brought for a מנחה are the wood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The לבונה is just as good a candidate. That reading would make blood, which comes with נסכים, need salt.

steps.title: Libations go with the burned parts, not the blood
steps.stepSummary: The נסכים do not belong to the blood. They go with the אימורין, because together these are the altar's 'eating and drinking.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The נסכים come along with the parts burned on the מזבח, not with the blood. Why? Burning the parts is like eating, and pouring the wine is like drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends itself. Blood does not have 'other items' with it, because the נסכים are connected to the אימורין and not to the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if we read 'other items' as לבונה, blood would still not be included, since the נסכים are not attached to it. Eating and drinking naturally go together, so the wine goes with the burned meat parts.

keyTerms.meaning: The fats and parts of an animal offering burned on the מזבח
Eating and drinking
Together with

phrases.english: The libations come together with the sacrificial parts,
What is the reason? Eating and drinking.
phrases.notes: Burning the parts is like the מזבח 'eating,' and pouring the wine is like it 'drinking,' so the two belong together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by denying that blood has accompanying items
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the link: the נסכים belong to the אימורין, not the blood
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood comes with נסכים, so it would count as something with 'other items'
steps.terutzMaskana: The נסכים are linked to the אימורין as eating and drinking, so blood has no accompanying items

steps.title: On the contrary: libations go with the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer. Blood brings atonement and the wine brings joy, so the נסכים really do go with the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just the opposite! First the blood brings atonement, and then the wine brings joy. So the נסכים do belong with the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from Step 22 with a counter-pairing, which brings back the challenge of Step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a pairing just as natural as 'eating and drinking': you first gain כפרה through the blood, then you celebrate with wine. That links the נסכים to the blood. So blood could still count as having 'other items.'

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Atonement, which the blood brings
Joy, expressed through the wine

phrases.english: On the contrary: atonement and joy!
phrases.notes: The blood brings atonement, and then the wine brings joy, so the wine fits together with the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 22's answer
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the נסכים belong only with the אימורין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An equally strong pairing (atonement then joy) links the נסכים to the blood

steps.title: Frankincense shares one vessel, but wood serves every offering
steps.stepSummary: The לבונה is special because it comes in the same כלי as the מנחה, which blood and נסכים do not. Wood, however, is needed for every קרבן, so the wood reading works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the לבונה comes together with the מנחה in one כלי, and blood does not share a כלי with the נסכים. But wood: just as a מנחה is made fit with wood, all קרבנות are made fit with wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer for why the 'other items' cannot be the לבונה, and it explains why the wood reading is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the model were the לבונה, the shared feature would be 'an extra item in the same כלי,' and blood would not qualify. Wood is different: every קרבן needs wood to be burned, so it works as a feature that spreads to all offerings. This is why Step 20's wood answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: One vessel
Wood used to burn offerings on the מזבח
Are made fit, meaning valid for use

phrases.english: Rather, the frankincense comes with it in one vessel,

phrases.english: but wood: just as a meal offering is made fit through it,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the models: the לבונה's link is unique (one כלי), while wood applies to all offerings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'other items' could be the לבונה, which would include blood
steps.terutzMaskana: The לבונה shares a כלי with the מנחה, which the נסכים do not do with the blood. Wood makes every קרבן fit, so the wood reading is correct
steps.whatToRemember: The 'other items' of the מנחה are the wood. Wood is used for every קרבן, unlike the לבונה, which shares one כלי with the מנחה.

steps.title: Maybe salt is needed only for something that also permits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests narrowing the rule: maybe only something that both needs other items and permits something else needs salt. That would include only the לבונה of the בזיכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this: the detail, the קומץ, has two features. Other items come for it, and it permits the rest of the מנחה. So only something with both features needs salt. What is that? The לבונה in the bowls, which permits the לחם הפנים. Nothing else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how widely the rule was applied. It suggests that the comparison should require both features of the קומץ, not just one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ needs wood, and it also makes the rest of the מנחה permitted to eat. If both features are required, regular animal parts would not need salt. Only the לבונה of the בזיכין, which permits the לחם הפנים, would.

keyTerms.meaning: The specific detail mentioned in the פסוק, here the מנחה or קומץ
It permits something else
The bowls of לבונה placed with the לחם הפנים
The showbread kept on the שולחן in the משכן and בית המקדש

phrases.english: But say: just as the detail is clearly defined,
as something for which other items come as a requirement, and that permits,

phrases.english: so too anything for which other items come as a requirement and that permits,
and what is that? The frankincense that comes in the bowls,

phrases.aramaic: דְּשָׁרְיָא לֶחֶם, אֲבָל מִידֵּי אַחֲרִינָא – לָא.
phrases.english: since it permits the bread, but anything else, no.

steps.kashyaTarget: The broad inclusion of everything burned with wood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פרט has two features. The comparison should require both, which would limit salt to the לבונה of the בזיכין

steps.title: Excluding blood proves one shared feature is enough
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק had to exclude blood with 'מעל מנחתך, and not from your blood.' Blood shares only the permitting feature, so this proves that one feature is enough to be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק needed to say 'from your מנחה,' to teach 'not from your blood.' That shows that all these items are included by matching the מנחה in just one way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 25 by pointing to the פסוק's need to exclude blood, and concludes that sharing one feature is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood permits the meat to be eaten, but it is not burned with wood, so it matches the קומץ in only one way. If both features were needed, blood would never have been included, and the פסוק would not need to exclude it. Since the פסוק did exclude it, one shared feature must be enough to include something.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it was necessary
By implication, it follows that
One aspect, one shared feature

steps.whatToRemember: An item needs salt if it matches the קומץ in even one feature. That is why the פסוק had to exclude blood specifically.

phrases.english: Since it was necessary to write 'from your meal offering,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:13

phrases.english: and not from your blood,

phrases.english: this implies that all these are included through one shared aspect.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאִיצְטְרִיךְ מֵעַל מִנְחָתֶךָ וְלֹא מֵעַל דָּמֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a verse's exclusion: the exclusion would be pointless unless one feature were enough

steps.terutzMaskana: Blood had to be excluded even though it shares only the permitting feature. So one shared feature is enough to require salt

steps.title: Why exclude blood and not the limbs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's reading 'from your מנחה, not from your blood' and asks why we should not say 'not from your limbs' instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'From your מנחה,' meaning salt is needed there, but not on your blood. But why not say: 'From your מנחה,' but not on your limbs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא and challenges it. The words 'and not from your blood' are not written in the פסוק, so why pick blood as the thing left out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 showed that the פסוק must leave something out of the salt rule, and the ברייתא said it was blood. But the limbs of an עולה are also offered on the מזבח, so they could just as easily be the thing left out. The גמרא wants a reason for choosing blood.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From your meal offering', the פסוק's words about not leaving out salt
Your blood, meaning the blood of a קרבן
Your limbs, meaning the parts of an animal קרבן burned on the מזבח

'From your meal offering', and not from your blood.

phrases.english: But say: 'From your meal offering'
and not from your limbs?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: מֵעַל מִנְחָתֶךָ וְלֹא מֵעַל אֵיבָרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's line in step 9, 'מעל מנחתך ולא מעל דמך', which step 26 also used, and questions why blood was the item excluded.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading 'and not from your blood'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק does not name what it leaves out, so the exclusion could just as well be the limbs instead of blood.

steps.title: The limbs are much more like a מנחה than blood
steps.stepSummary: It makes more sense to include the limbs, because they share six features with a מנחה: other items are needed for them, they go on the fire, they are offered on the outer מזבח, and the rules of נותר, טומאה and מעילה apply to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the limbs should be included, since (memory aid: א״ש בנטמ״א) other items come as a requirement for them, like a מנחה; they go on the fire, like a מנחה; they are offered outside, like a מנחה; the rule of leftovers applies, like a מנחה; the rule of impurity applies, like a מנחה; the rule of misusing holy property applies, like a מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the limbs are very similar to a מנחה, so they belong in the salt rule, and blood is the one left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a פסוק leaves something out, we leave out whatever is least like the main case. The limbs match the מנחה in six ways, and blood matches in almost none of them. So the limbs are included and blood is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes sense
To include in the rule
A memory aid made of letters
The fire of the מזבח
Leftover parts of a קרבן past their time, which are forbidden
Misusing holy property

steps.whatToRemember: Blood is left out of the salt rule, and the limbs are kept in, because the limbs share six features with the מנחה (א״ש בנטמ״א) and blood does not.

phrases.english: It stands to reason,
the limbs are what he should include,
since (memory aid: א״ש בנטמ״א)
phrases.notes: Each letter stands for one shared feature listed next: אחרים, אישים, בחוץ, נותר, טומאה, מעילה.

phrases.english: other items come as a requirement for it, like the meal offering,
it goes on the fire, like it; it is offered outside, like it;
phrases.notes: 'Outside' means the outer מזבח. Some blood is brought inside the היכל, for example on יום הכפורים.

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתָר כְּמוֹתָהּ, טוּמְאָה כְּמוֹתָהּ, מְעִילָה כְּמוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: leftovers apply, like it; impurity applies, like it; misuse of holy property applies, like it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by showing why blood, not the limbs, is the one left out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparing features: the item more like the main case is included, and the less similar one is excluded.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exclusion in the פסוק could just as easily refer to the limbs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limbs share six features with a מנחה, so they need salt, and the exclusion must be blood.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the limbs of a קרבן are salted on the מזבח while blood is not.
